traces.name: mock_merge_intervals
traces.title: Write merge_intervals against a visible test suite
traces.note: The programming setting. Every node is a complete program and the reward is the fraction of tests it passes, so simulation is skipped. The one-pass approach looks best to the model and caps at three of five; the fix is a different branch, not a better patch.

traces.name: mock_game_of_24
traces.title: Game of 24
traces.note: All six operations, including simulation: the tree descends greedily by value, in the real environment, until one number is left. Solved on the fifth iteration, after four dead ends.

traces.name: mock_game_of_24_no_value
traces.title: Game of 24
traces.note: Ablation: lambda = 0, so V(s) is self-consistency alone and the model's own judgement is thrown away. It still gets there, but it needs every iteration it has and half again as many nodes.

traces.name: mock_game_of_24_greedy
traces.title: Game of 24
traces.note: Ablation: w = 0, so UCT collapses to pure exploitation and selection never leaves the branch it liked first. It grows a larger tree than the full search and never finds 24 at all.

traces.name: mock_game_of_24_hard
traces.title: Game of 24, the hard one
traces.note: 6, 9, 9, 10, where the twelve best-looking first moves are all dead ends and every solution ends in 9 + 15. The offline policy rates a fraction badly and never proposes the moves that reach 15, so sixteen iterations of correct search find nothing. Search cannot choose what the policy never suggests - compare the OpenAI run on the same puzzle.

traces.name: mock_multihop_qa
traces.title: Two-hop question answering with a retrieval tool
traces.note: Two-hop retrieval. The corpus holds a tempting near-miss answer, and the policy has a recency bias that walks straight into it; the second iteration backs out and finds the right document.

traces.name: mock_multihop_qa_no_reflection
traces.title: Two-hop question answering with a retrieval tool
traces.note: Ablation: reflection off. Identical outcome, one step shorter - which is the paper's own finding. Reflection is the smallest of its three ablations; the value function and the search structure matter more.

traces.name: openai_game_of_24
traces.title: Game of 24
traces.note: gpt-5 on the easy puzzle, and the honest counterexample. It proposes a winning first move straight away, the rollout confirms it, and the search is over in one iteration - nothing is ever backtracked, marked down or reflected on. When the policy already knows the answer, tree search buys nothing but tokens. Read it next to mock_game_of_24, which needs five iterations and forty-five nodes to reach the same place.

traces.name: openai_game_of_24_hard
traces.title: Game of 24, the hard one
traces.note: gpt-5 searching correctly for sixteen iterations and getting nowhere, which is the most useful failure in this set. Its five root proposals are the tidy ones - 9-6, 9/9, 9+9, 10-6, 6+10 - and not one of them can reach 24; every solution needs 9*10=90 or a fraction. Selection, backpropagation and reflection all work perfectly on a tree that cannot contain the answer. LATS searches what the policy proposes, and cannot repair a policy that never proposes it. The offline run on this puzzle picks almost the same five moves.

traces.name: openai_game_of_24_hard_wide
traces.title: Game of 24, the hard one
traces.note: The same model and the same puzzle as openai_game_of_24_hard, with one knob moved: twelve samples per expansion instead of five. That is enough for 9*10=90 to appear among the root's children - the only winning move gpt-5 proposes - and everything else follows from the search. Watch the exploitation column: 9*10 sits at the bottom of it for seven iterations while selection works through 6*9, 9/9, 6+10, 10-9, 10-6 and 6+9, each returning reward 0 and each marked down by backpropagation. On iteration eight the exploration bonus reaches 1.44, the largest term on the board, and carries selection into the branch nothing liked. Reward 1. The UCT tug-of-war doing its whole job, one step at a time.

traces.name: openai_multihop_qa
traces.title: Two-hop question answering with a retrieval tool
traces.note: gpt-5 on two-hop retrieval: the whole LATS loop in thirteen steps. The first trajectory commits to ECML 2006, the environment scores it 0, backpropagation marks that branch down and reflection writes the wrong answer off by name. The second iteration selects elsewhere and lands on the right document. The shortest trace here that still shows every operation doing its job.
